questions.question: Dr. Amrani, a dental surgeon, operates his practice as a single-member LLC. According to Article 1 of Law 9-88, who is required to keep accounting records?
options: Only publicly traded companies
Any natural or legal person with the status of merchant under the Commercial Code
Only public legal entities
Only chartered accountants
questions.explanation: Art. 1: the law applies to any natural or legal person with merchant status under the Commercial Code — a practice operating company falls within this scope.

questions.question: Dr. Amrani's practice generates an annual turnover of 1.5 million DH. Which simplified regime under Article 1 can he claim?
options: None, the exemption threshold is 500,000 DH
Chronological and overall recording, day by day, of transactions at their receipt or payment date
Total exemption from any accounting
Obligation to keep an accounting manual
questions.explanation: Art. 1, para. 5: natural persons whose annual turnover does not exceed 2,000,000 DH benefit from a simplified chronological recording at receipt/payment.

questions.question: What is the annual turnover threshold mentioned in Article 1 below which a natural person may simplify their accounting (except insurance agents)?
questions.explanation: Art. 1, para. 5: threshold of 2,000,000 DH.

questions.question: Dr. Bennani, a dentist practicing as a sole proprietor with a turnover of 1.8 million DH, wishes to record his receivables and payables at year-end. What does the law provide for him?
options: He must keep a detailed general ledger
He may record them globally on a summary list mentioning the identity of clients/suppliers and the amount of their debts
He is prohibited from recording receivables and payables
He must have this list certified by a chartered accountant
questions.explanation: Art. 1, para. 5, 2nd bullet.

questions.question: According to Article 2, in which register are accounting entries first recorded?
options: The general ledger
The inventory book
The journal
The accounting manual
questions.explanation: Art. 2, para. 1: entries are recorded in a register called the 'journal'.

questions.question: According to Article 2, every accounting entry must respect which fundamental principle?
options: It must affect at least two accounts, one debited and one credited with the same amount
It must affect only one account
It must be validated by the court clerk before recording
It must be expressed in foreign currency
questions.explanation: Art. 2, para. 2: double-entry principle.

questions.question: Is Dr. Amrani's practice (LLC, turnover of 4 million DH) exempt from keeping a general ledger?
options: Yes, all companies are exempt
No, only natural persons referred to in Article 1, paragraph 5 (turnover ≤ 2,000,000 DH) may be exempt, under certain conditions
Yes, from 3 million DH in turnover
No, the general ledger has been completely abolished by law
questions.explanation: Art. 2, last paragraph: exemption reserved for natural persons referred to in Art. 1, para. 5, if the trial balance can be established directly from the journal.

questions.question: According to Article 3, how often must entries recorded in subsidiary journals and ledgers be centralized in the journal and general ledger?
options: Once a week
Once a month
Once a quarter
Once per financial year only
questions.explanation: Art. 3, para. 2: monthly centralization, in principle.

questions.question: Dr. Bennani (natural person, turnover ≤ 2,000,000 DH) may centralize his subsidiary journals according to which derogatory frequency provided for in Article 3?
options: Once a week
Once a month like everyone else
Once per financial year, at its close
He is not entitled to deferred centralization
questions.explanation: Art. 3, last paragraph.

questions.question: If the dental practice constituted as a company generates an annual turnover of 12 million DH, what does Article 4 require?
options: Nothing special, the relevant threshold is 20 million
The establishment of a manual describing the company's accounting organization
The mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor
Keeping accounts in foreign currency
questions.explanation: Art. 4: obligation of an accounting organization manual above 10,000,000 DH in turnover.

questions.question: According to Article 5, how often must the inventory of the company's assets and liabilities be carried out?
options: Once a month
Once a quarter
At least once per financial year, at its end
Once every two financial years
questions.explanation: Art. 5.

questions.question: What must the inventory book mentioned in Article 6 record?
options: Only the list of dental equipment
The balance sheet and income statement for each financial year
Only customer receivables
Only the list of suppliers
questions.explanation: Art. 6.

questions.question: What is the normal duration of the accounting period according to Article 7?
options: 6 months
9 months
12 months
18 months
questions.explanation: Art. 7: 12 months, except for exceptions (exceptionally shorter periods).

questions.question: According to Article 8, who must generally number and initial the practice's journal and inventory book?
options: The President of the National Order of Dental Surgeons
The court clerk of the court of first instance of the company's registered office
The tax inspector
A notary
questions.explanation: Art. 8, para. 1.

questions.question: Is Dr. Bennani (turnover ≤ 2,000,000 DH) required to have his books numbered and initialed by the court clerk?
options: Yes, without any exception
No, provided he keeps the books, balance sheet, and income statement for ten years
No, this obligation only applies to public limited companies
Yes, but only every five years
questions.explanation: Art. 8, last paragraph.

questions.question: According to Article 9, which documents together form the annual financial statements?
options: Only the balance sheet and tax return
The balance sheet, income statement, management balance sheet, financing statement, and supplementary information statement
Only the income statement
The business license and professional tax
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 2: these 5 documents form an inseparable whole.

questions.question: According to Article 10, what exactly does the dental practice's balance sheet describe?
options: Only the year's receipts
Separately the assets and liabilities of the enterprise
The number of patients received
The monthly turnover
questions.explanation: Art. 10, para. 1.

questions.question: According to Article 10, what principle governs the income statement's summary of revenue and expenses?
options: Regardless of their receipt or payment date
Only cash transactions
Only social security contributions (CNSS)
Only supplier invoice dates
questions.explanation: Art. 10, para. 2: accrual basis, not cash basis.

questions.question: What must the financial statements provide according to the principle stated in Article 11?
options: An approximate estimate of income
A true and fair view of the assets, liabilities, financial position, and results of the enterprise
Only a snapshot of available cash
A budget projection for the following financial year
questions.explanation: Art. 11: true and fair view principle.

questions.question: According to Article 13, can the presentation of financial statements and the valuation methods adopted by the practice change freely each year?
options: Yes, without any constraint
No, they cannot be changed from one financial year to another, unless described and justified in the supplementary information statement
Yes, provided the court clerk is informed
No, they are definitively fixed upon the practice's creation
questions.explanation: Art. 13: principle of consistency of methods.

questions.question: Dr. Amrani purchases a new dental chair for consideration. According to Article 14, at what value should he record it upon entry into the business?
options: At its estimated resale value
At its acquisition cost
At its insured value
At the supplier's list price, excluding discounts
questions.explanation: Art. 14, para. 1: assets acquired for consideration → acquisition cost.

questions.question: This same dental chair, a fixed asset with a limited useful life, must be subject to which value adjustment according to Article 14?
options: A provision for risks only
Depreciation, spreading its depreciable amount over its expected useful life
No adjustment, medical equipment is exempt
An annual mandatory revaluation by an expert
questions.explanation: Art. 14, para. 4-5.

questions.question: According to Article 14, what simplified method may Dr. Bennani (natural person, turnover ≤ 2,000,000 DH) use to calculate depreciation of his equipment?
options: A simplified straight-line method
A complex declining balance method is mandatory
No simplification is provided for depreciation
Only the units of production method
questions.explanation: Art. 14, last paragraph, 2nd bullet.

questions.question: According to Article 15, can an asset item be offset against a liability item in the practice's balance sheet?
options: Yes, it is even recommended to simplify reading
No, no offsetting may be made between asset and liability items, nor between income and expenses
Yes, but only for small amounts
Yes, if the chartered accountant authorizes it
questions.explanation: Art. 15, para. 3: prohibition of offsetting.

questions.question: According to Article 18, within what maximum timeframe must the practice's financial statements be prepared after the close of the financial year (except for duly justified exceptional circumstances)?
options: 1 month
3 months
6 months
12 months
questions.explanation: Art. 18, para. 1: 3-month deadline.

questions.question: If the dental practice (as a company) generates an annual turnover of 8 million DH, what does Article 21 provide?
options: It must mandatorily prepare all 5 complete financial statements
It is exempt from the management balance sheet, financing statement, and supplementary information statement, and may use the simplified model
It is totally exempt from the balance sheet
It must have its accounts certified by two chartered accountants
questions.explanation: Art. 21: exemption for taxpayers whose turnover ≤ 10,000,000 DH.

questions.question: For how many years must the practice's accounting documents and supporting documents be kept, according to Article 22?
options: 3 years
5 years
10 years
20 years
questions.explanation: Art. 22, para. 2: retention for ten years.

questions.question: According to Article 23, what can the tax authorities do if the practice's accounting is not kept in the forms prescribed by Law 9-88?
options: They must accept it if VAT has been paid
They may reject this accounting
They can do nothing without a prior court decision
They must only notify the National Order of Dental Surgeons
questions.explanation: Art. 23: power of rejection by the tax authorities.

questions.question: If Dr. Amrani entrusts his accounting to a chartered accountant or approved accountant, what does Article 24 impose on them?
options: No particular constraints, they are free to use their own methods
They are required to comply with the provisions of Law 9-88 and its appendix for the accounting of the enterprises they handle
They must apply only IFRS standards
They must obtain prior court clerk approval for each entry
questions.explanation: Art. 24.
